subject: ForgeBank: rack zoning & ephemeral-to-block migration for model caches
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@forgebank.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Infra Support <infra-support@forgebank.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: ForgeBank: rack zoning and storage question for private deployment

Hi Vivek / Laura —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re starting readiness planning for ForgeBank’s private deployment and hit two questions that will determine our hardware layout and storage choices: rack zoning strategy across two data halls, and whether we can rely on ephemeral NVMe for model cache + WAL, or if we need block-backed PVs for those tiers.

Summary of constraints (attached: site-inventory.csv):
- 2 data halls (A/B) connected by 10G redundant fabric, cross-rack latency ~120us
- 48 servers total: mix of 4x A100 nodes (32GB) and 44 x 4xA10g (permanent inference)
- Limited on-prem SAN (iSCSI) available but shared with existing infra — prefer local NVMe for perf
- Compliance: WAL retention and audit logs cannot be lost; backups run nightly to S3-compatible vault

Primary asks:
1) Do we recommend node-affinity / rack-aware PV topology for model cache + PG WAL?
2) If ephemeral NVMe is used for hot model caches, what fallback plan do you recommend for node failure?
3) Any required kubelet or eviction thresholds to protect model cache eviction during bursts?

We’d like a short decision doc we can share with infra ops by next Wednesday (Dec 23).

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Infrastructure, ForgeBank

Attachments: site-inventory.csv (csv)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-18T12:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ForgeBank: rack zoning and storage question for private deployment

Laura / Aditya —

Quick internal run-through before I reply to Sam with a concise plan. High level recommendations I’m thinking:

1) Node pools and rack zoning
  - control-plane (3 nodes spread across halls A/B, avoid colocating all control-plane in single hall)
  - inference-hot: on local NVMe nodes (fast local-ssd / ephemeral) sized for model memory + KV cache (daemonset-managed prefetch)
  - inference-persistent: block-backed PVs (CSI LVM or iSCSI) for PG WAL, long-lived model artifacts and checkpoints
  - model-cache-proxy (statefulset) with PVCs that use ReadWriteMany where possible for read-only replicas (or duplicated blockstore objects)

2) Storage class / PV binding
  - Fast-local-nvme storageclass for ephemeral workloads; set volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer and topology keys to match rack labels (kubernetes.io/hostname & topology.kubernetes.io/zone)
  - Blockstore-class (replicated) for critical data (WAL, metadata). Use RWO with synchronous replication at the block layer (or replicate at application level for PG)

3) Availability/failover for ephemeral model caches
  - Treat ephemeral NVMe as cache-only: lost cache must be recomputable from blockstore or object-store; ensure model fetch & warm-up is automated on pod start
  - Keep a small persistent model-cache tier on blockstore for the N most-frequently-used models (serves as bootstraps)
  - Use node affinity and pod anti-affinity so we don’t place all hot replicas on same rack

4) Kubelet / eviction recommendations
  - Reserve ephemeral disk via eviction threshold: eviction-hard: nodefs.available<10% and imagefs.available<15% (adjust after load testing)
  - Set kube-reserved and system-reserved to leave >15% disk headroom for kubelet + logs

5) Operational items
  - Daily healthcheck to ensure model cache warming completes within 5 minutes after pod restart; use a probe that validates model checksum + inference latency
  - Pre-signed objectstore fallback for model artifacts if blockstore becomes degraded

I’ll draft a concise note for Sam with those bullets and attach PV class guidance doc; can you both scan for missing compliance or HA items? I’ll send to ForgeBank and ask for site-level NIC topology diagram (they attached a coarse inventory but not rack-to-switch mappings).

Attachments I’ll include: pv-class-recommendations.pdf (draft).

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@forgebank.com>, Infra Support <infra-support@forgebank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-19T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ForgeBank: rack zoning and storage question for private deployment

Sam —

Thanks for the inventory. Based on what you sent, here’s a short, actionable plan we recommend for your on-prem Kubernetes deployment. We kept it minimal so you can share with ops quickly.

Decision summary (for team share / infra runbook):

A) Node pools & rack zoning (two-datacenter aware)
  - Hall A / Hall B: label nodes with topology.kubernetes.io/zone=hall-a / hall-b and rack IDs (rack=ra1, ra2, rb1, rb2)
  - Control plane: 3 control-plane nodes split 2x in Hall A, 1x in Hall B (or vice-versa depending on existing maintenance windows)
  - inference-hot (NVMe-local): place on subset of servers with local NVMe, set nodeSelector: hardware=nvme-hot; use PodAntiAffinity to spread across racks
  - inference-persistent: on nodes that can mount blockstore; use storageclass: blockstore-replicated with topology constraints to prefer local hall replicas

B) Storage classes & PV strategy
  - storageclass: fast-local-nvme (volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, reclaimPolicy: Delete) — for model caches only
  - storageclass: blockstore-replicated (RWO, synchronous replication at block layer where available) — for WAL and checkpoints
  - PVC topology: use volume node affinity and allowedTopologies to tie PVs to racks when strict locality is required (e.g., local SSD for low-latency inference)

C) Cache durability pattern
  - Ephemeral NVMe = cache. Design apps so cache loss is acceptable and model rehydration pulls from blockstore or objectstore (S3-compatible)
  - Persist critical artifacts (WAL, audit logs, model metadata) to blockstore; replicate nightly offsite to S3 vault
  - Keep a lightweight persistent model tier (small PVCs) for fastest warm-starts of top N models

D) Kubelet + eviction tuning (starting values — validate under load)
  - kube-reserved: cpu=200m,memory=512Mi,ephemeral-storage=2Gi
  - system-reserved: cpu=200m,memory=512Mi,ephemeral-storage=2Gi
  - eviction-hard: memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10% ,imagefs.available<15%
  - pod eviction priority: mark model-cache pods as lower-priority (interruptible) than inference-serving pods if throughput matters more than cold-start latency

E) Failover & recovery
  - Automated model prefetch & background rehydration on pod launch; health probe gated by model checksum + sample inference
  - For PG WAL, use Patroni or equivalent with synchronous replicas across racks; ensure restart scripts push WAL to blockstore quickly

Action items (owners):
  - ForgeBank: provide rack-to-switch mapping + 1U/2U layout by Dec 21 (Infra Support)
  - Redwood (Vivek): annotate PV class doc and share topologies (done) — see drive link below
  - Redwood (Laura): run a short failure-recovery sim with your test cluster to validate eviction thresholds (by Dec 23)

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/forgebank/plan-2026-12 (contains pv-class-recommendations.pdf and node-affinity diagram)

We’re attaching a short PV class recommendation PDF and a small node affinity diagram for your ops team. If you want, we can run a 30-minute call with your infra ops to walk the operators through the node labels and PVC binding behavior.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pv-class-recommendations.pdf (pdf), forgebank-node-affinity-diagram.png (png)

Subject: Re: ForgeBank: rack zoning and storage question for private deployment

Vivek —

This looks good and pragmatic. A couple of follow-ups from infra ops:
1) Cross-rack peering: our switch team prefers to avoid synchronous block replication across halls due to cost; they suggested async replication with a short RPO for WAL. Is that acceptable?
2) They also asked for concrete kubelet eviction numbers tied to our 800GB NVMe nodes. Can you propose a floor for imagefs/nodefs for those sizes?

If we accept async replication for blockstore, we’ll put an extra persistent model-cache replica in Hall B (small PVC) to reduce cold-start impact.

Thanks,
Sam

On a side note: Maya from Finance also asked whether this architecture will change our procurement timeline — I’ll loop her if needed.
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@forgebank.com>, Infra Support <infra-support@forgebank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ForgeBank: rack zoning and storage question for private deployment — final recommendations

Sam / Infra team —

Short answers:
1) Async replication for blockstore is acceptable if combined with:
   - fast local WAL shipping to blockstore and more frequent DB checkpoints, and
   - a small persistent model-cache replica in the opposite hall (Hall B) to reduce cold-start tail latency.

2) Kubelet eviction numbers (for 800GB NVMe nodes, suggested starting point):
   - kube-reserved ephemeral-storage: 10Gi
   - system-reserved ephemeral-storage: 8Gi
   - eviction-hard: imagefs.available<12%, nodefs.available<8%
   - target headroom: keep ~80-100Gi free for transient spikes in model downloads/logging during heavy churn

We endorse the plan in the Dec 19 note with the small change above. Next steps:
  - Infra Support: provide rack-to-switch mapping and confirm if you’ll accept async block replication (reply here)
  - Redwood: we’ll schedule a 30-minute run-through with your ops (suggest Dec 28 or Jan 4) to step through node labels, PVC binding, and recovery playbook

If you’re comfortable, consider this our decision record and we’ll add a short entry to the onboarding doc (HUBSPOT-Deal-4321).

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
